title: Tentpole priming and rate-smoothing for GPU pool stability
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We observed a sustained hosted API tenant surge that exhausted a subset of GPU pools, producing long request queues and aggressive throttling for best-effort traffic. The immediate mitigation (emergency scale-up + consumer throttle) restored availability but exposed two recurring weaknesses: unstable autoscaler hysteresis for bursty inference workloads, and amplification of queue buildup from bursty prefetch/pipeline traffic that bypassed steady admission controls.

Scope / Impact:
- Incident window: 2025-10-28 03:12 UTC — 2025-10-28 05:07 UTC (primary disruption).
- Affected: ~12% of hosted customers saw elevated latency and 503s for generation requests. High-traffic tenants experienced request drops and degraded SLOs.
- Root cause (summary): autoscaler cooldown and slot accounting combined with a short-lived traffic fanout pattern from a single large tenant. Prefetch spikes generated many short-lived requests that inflated per-GPU queue depth and prevented the autoscaler from making stable scale decisions.

Investigation highlights and evidence:
- Traces: request fanout patterns visible in tracing (trace IDs: trace-20251028-03a, trace-20251028-03b).
- Metrics: per-GPU queue depth rose > 10x baseline; autoscaler did not trigger until queue depth sustained above threshold for 90s due to conservative smoothing.
- Repro: synthetic load generator reproduces queue amplification when prefetch ratio > 4 and request size variance > 3x. Test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-load-tests/pull/197

Decisions / Design proposals:
1) Tentpole priming: keep a small pool of pre-provisioned slots in each GPU pool that can be instantly allocated for bursts while respecting tenant isolation. This reduces cold-queue buildup and reduces the amplification effect.
2) Rate-smoothing admission: add a leaky-bucket per-tenant admission layer that smooths ingress peaks to the serving runtime and applies a short, soft backpressure window before hard rejection. Soft backpressure behavior should be tunable per-plan (free/dev/prod).
3) Autoscaler tuning: reduce scale-out detection smoothing window from 90s -> 30s for generation-heavy pools, add opportunistic prewarm policy that primes nodes when admission queue exceeds a moving average threshold for N tenants.
4) Prefetch isolation: enforce stricter budget for prefetch/pipeline requests (separate admission tokens) to avoid crowding real-time requests during bursts.

Action items (owners + target dates):
- A: Implement tentpole priming controller (Liam) — spike implementation by 2025-11-10, full rollout 2025-12-01. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3218
- B: Rate-smoothing admission (Asha) — prototype 2025-11-07, integrate with tenant-tier configs 2025-11-20. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/admission/pull/142
- C: Autoscaler policy change and testing harness (Nina) — policy change merged 2025-11-12, end-to-end stress test 2025-11-18. Issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/issues/88
- D: Prefetch budget enforcement (Platform team) — telemetry and enforcement rules 2025-11-15. Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Prefetch+Isolation
- E: Runbook updates & alerts (SRE: Marco) — new alerts for queue skew and tentpole depletion 2025-11-09. Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/GPU+Pool+Queue+Runbook

Metrics to track post rollout:
- 95th/99th latency for generation requests per-pool (goal: 50% reduction in queue-induced latency spikes).
- Frequency and duration of pool queue depth > X (goal: reduce events by 80% over next quarter).
- Tentpole utilization and time-to-request-satisfaction after priming.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Stage rollout: dev -> canary (5% traffic) -> pool-limited (targeted pools) -> global. Monitor canary for unexpected tenant fairness regressions.
- E2E stress tests using the synthetic harness to validate smoothing knobs and tentpole limits across traffic patterns (short spikes, long sustained load, heavy prefetch).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Tentpole sizing heuristics: static small fraction vs. adaptive fraction based on recent variance. We'll start with static (2% of slots) and iterate to adaptive.
- Tenant fairness vs. latency: rate-smoothing can add small delay; need guardrails so paid tiers see minimal soft-backpressure.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Tentpole priming implemented + canary tested with no regression on tenant fairness.
- Rate-smoothing admission in prod for hosted pools with metrics demonstrating reduced queue amplification (compare pre/post stress runs).
- Autoscaler policy changes merged and validated by SRE stress runs.
- Runbook and alerting updated with clear escalation paths.

2025-11-08 - Nina Gomez: Autoscaler smoothing window experiment (30s) passed unit / integration tests. Observed faster scale-out but with slightly higher transient preemption. Working on opportunistic prewarm logic.

2025-11-15 - Asha Patel: Integrated tenant-tier config defaults for soft-backpressure. Added per-tenant telemetry labels to help debugging. Linked follow-up task to tune thresholds per plan.
2025-11-16 - Marco Ruiz: Alerting thresholds tuned after canary; added runbook step to temporarily increase tentpole on holiday launch windows.
2025-11-18 - Liam Chen: Moving to wider rollout for GPU pools in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Remaining: prefetch token budget enforcement (Platform team) and final autoscaler policy safety checks.
